name: agent-fs-permission-grants
body:
The agent-grant surface for the fs tools: the `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` template edits that generate each implementer's permission block with `apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp` granted deny-by-default (the tools' CALLABILITY gate), with every allow (and every deny) mirrored under `apg/.worktrees/*/`. That tool-level grant does NOT do per-path matching: the tools themselves self-enforce per-path scope from the acting agent's granted globs.

The template-edit surface is BOTH edits, not one:
- Rule 6 (`plain rm <path>` / `rm <dir>/*.<ext>`): replace the current shallow bash `rm` wording with the fs-tool path-scoped grants, so generated implementers stop relying on bash `rm` patterns and can implement `deletes`/`renames`/`moves` tasks.
- Rule 10 (worktree-mirrored grants): amend its tail exemption so it no longer lumps the path-scoped fs-tool glob grants together with cwd-agnostic bash patterns. Rule 10 currently says "Bash command patterns and tool grants need no variants (they are cwd-agnostic; the agents `cd` into the worktree)." — correct for bash command patterns, but WRONG for the `apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp` path globs, which opencode resolves against the session workspace root (the main checkout) exactly like edit globs, so they DO need the `apg/.worktrees/*/<glob>` variants. Rule 10 must either drop "and tool grants" from that exemption (stating that path-scoped tool grants are mirrored like edit globs) or explicitly carve out the exception: the exemption covers cwd-agnostic bash command patterns only, and the path-scoped fs-tool glob grants ARE mirrored under `apg/.worktrees/*/`.

Editing rule 6 alone leaves the template self-contradictory: rule 10 would still exempt the very grants rule 6 introduces, so an implementer told the grants are mirrored "per rule 10" would read rule 10's plain text as "no variants needed". Both edits are the surface.

It is product source in the opencode-suite distribution (`solution.container.opencode-suite`), installed by `apg init` into `~/.opencode/agents/`; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and are never edited by this change-set.

implemented-by: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`.
